title: 10 Voter Suppression Methods
summary: Josh and Chuck count down ten methods used to suppress voting in the United States, tracing them from Reconstruction and the Jim Crow South to recent years. They cover poll taxes, literacy tests and the Louisiana brain teaser test, grandfather clauses, violence by the Ku Klux Klan, registration hurdles and closed registration offices, voter intimidation (including the 2004 Florida trooper visits and the 2018 Georgia arrests of Brunswick-area officials), purging voter rolls (Florida 2000 and Georgia 2018), voter ID laws and their costs, closing polling places and early voting cuts (Texas, Maricopa County), deceptive mailers and robocalls (Virginia 2008, Maryland 2010, Mitch McConnell mailers 2014, Michigan and Chicago robocalls), and restrictions on voting by people with felony convictions (Florida Amendment 4 and the later fines-and-fees requirement). The hosts argue voter fraud is extremely rare, that these measures mainly burden Black, minority and poor voters, and that the 2013 Shelby County ruling weakened Section 5 of the Voting Rights Act. The episode ends with listener mail about fallout shelter signs in Topeka, Kansas.
topics: Stuff You Should Know top ten

segments.title: Opening and framing
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the top ten list and note an earlier episode on election laws. They argue that voting barriers conflict with democracy and that voter fraud is extremely rare.
topics: Stuff You Should Know top ten

segments.title: Poll taxes and literacy tests
segments.summary: The hosts describe poll taxes, starting with Virginia's tax, and how grandfather clauses exempted white voters. They then cover literacy tests, the Louisiana brain-teaser test, and their subjective administration by white poll workers.

segments.title: Violence and the Ku Klux Klan
segments.summary: The hosts describe violence and terror by groups such as the Ku Klux Klan as a way to deter Black voters and those who helped them register. They note that federal action came later and that more than 3,000 Klan members were indicted but about 600 convicted.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: The hosts take a break before continuing the list.
topics: Stuff You Should Know top ten

segments.title: Shelby County ruling and registration barriers
segments.summary: The hosts explain that Section 5 of the Voting Rights Act required federal review of voting changes until the 2013 Supreme Court ruling. They then describe registration hurdles such as address requirements, closed registration offices, and employers and boycotts that discouraged time off to register.

segments.title: Voter intimidation
segments.summary: The hosts discuss intimidation, including Florida state troopers questioning elderly Black voters in 2004 and the arrests of Georgia school board officials in 2014. They also cover a Mitch McConnell campaign mailer that looked like an official notice.

segments.title: Purging voter rolls and voter ID
segments.summary: The hosts describe purges of voter rolls in Florida before 2000 and in Georgia, where about 200,000 people were removed while Brian Kemp was secretary of state and a candidate. They then discuss voter ID laws and their costs, including fees and time off work.

segments.title: Polling place closures, early voting cuts and deceptive robocalls
segments.summary: The hosts cover closing polling places and cutting early voting in swing states, Maricopa County, and Texas, where mail ballot drop-off was limited to one site per county. They then describe deceptive flyers and robocalls, including the 2008 Virginia flyer and the 2010 Maryland robocall that led to a conviction of Paul Schurick.

segments.title: Felon disenfranchisement
segments.summary: The hosts discuss laws barring people with criminal convictions from voting. They cover Florida's 2018 Amendment 4 and the later legislature requirement that fines and fees be paid first.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: Listener Ellie from Topeka, Kansas writes about spotting a fallout shelter sign. The hosts close by urging listeners to check their registration and vote.
